name: web-refused
description: What a tool does when a page says no. The question is not whether it gets the content — nothing does — but whether the caller is told something it can act on. Judged against the WHOLE result rather than a text field, because the useful answer here is a status and a flag, not prose: a tool that throws has told the model only that something went wrong, and a tool that returns an empty success has told it something false.

cases.about: An explicit 403 with an empty body. A useful answer names the status and says what to try next.
A 404 is a fact about the URL, and the caller should be able to tell it apart from a network failure.
